Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is not a formal registration process to be taken into consideration. The process works by simply attending the courses in the first two weeks after the lectures have commenced. During those two weeks students are encouraged to attend as many courses of interest as possible, whereafter students choose their final courses within a given deadline by sending a confirmation to the faculty. There is a system for HU in general called "Agnes" which some faculties use for student registration, but the faculty of law does not use that (status as per the summer semester 2023).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In all honesty, I would not pretend that I befriended many of the local students. I believe that it is a misconception that the purpose of an exchange semester is socializing with the local students. Most students would not befriend exchange students knowing that they would already leave the city in four months, i.e. it is often a wasted effort and not build to last. In short, I would recommend future exchange students to accept the fact that they will most likely only socialize with the other exchange students, which is also very nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you choose the courses taught in German, you do not have to stress about the oral exams as the lecturers will go easy on you. 
2. Choose a few of the courses which can be completed over the course of two weekends. 
3. The semester will most likely end in the end of July, regardless of the official semester dates reaching into September.
